div.head: Ordal 1a
div.ab: ⁊ béo þǽr gemeten nygon fét of þam stácan to þære mearce be þæs mannes fótan, þe þártó gæð.
Et sint mensurati IX pedes a staca usque ad mercam, ad mensuram pedum eius, qui ad iudicium ire debet.
and béo þǽr gemeten nygon fét of þam stácan to þære mearce be þæs mannes fótan, þe þártó gæð.
1a. Und es werde da 9 Fuss, gemäss des Mannes Füssen, der dort zu[m Ordal] schreiten wird, ausgemessen von den Pfählen (dem Pfahle?) bis zum Ziele.
1a. And let 9 feet be measured there, by the feet of the man who will go to [the ordeal], from the stakes (the stake?) to the mark.
And from the stake to the mark, nine feet shall be measured by the feet of him who goes to the trial.

note.seg: Den regulären Sing. nehmen an Q, auch 5, 1 und Toller s. v. Beim späten Zeitalter H's könnte auch Plural gemeint sein. Dies nimmt Q 4, 2 an
Q assumes the regular sing., as also at 5, 1, and so does Toller s. v. Given H's late date, the plural could also be meant. Q assumes this at 4, 2
Nach des Prüflings Fuss misst auch Indisches Eisenordal; Kaegi in Festschr. 39. Versa. Dt. Philolo. Zürich 48. Auch Ags. Zaubersegen ähneln Altindischen; Schröer Grundz. Engl. Lit. G. I 34²

The Indian iron ordeal also measures by the foot of the person undergoing it; Kaegi in Festschr. 39. Versa. Dt. Philolo. Zürich 48. Anglo-Saxon charms also resemble Old Indian ones; Schröer Grundz. Engl. Lit. G. I 34²
cf. § 4. The iron had to be carried from the stake (post) to the mark which defined the distance.
